title: IMF chief urges countries to do more to curb debt and regulate AI
source_used: Associated Press (wire copy read on Bozeman Daily Chronicle; apnews.com returned 403)
key_facts: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva gave a speech in Singapore on Wednesday, 7 Oct 2026, ahead of the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok next week.
She said countries rich and poor must act faster to cut debt and reduce inequality, as the AI boom, heavy borrowing and wars in the Middle East and Ukraine strain their economies.
She warned that AI investment has a lag before benefits arrive, and that if earnings fall short, hyperscaler leverage and US equity holdings could turn a disappointment into a far-reaching shock.
Seven of the top 10 countries for AI-related trade are in Asia-Pacific, a region whose share of global economic activity rose to 43% from 25% in 1991.
She urged governments to contain public spending, raise borrowing costs if needed to control inflation, and ensure AI is well regulated.
She said AI is also raising energy demand and pushing up prices for fuel, fertiliser and food.
quote_evidence: Countries both rich and poor must take faster action to cut debt and counter growing inequality as their economies weather a triple whammy from the artificial intelligence boom, heavy borrowing and shocks from wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, the head of the IMF said Wednesday.
"Should earnings fall short," she said, "hyperscaler leverage and large and growing global holdings of U.S. equities could turn a disappointment into a far-reaching shock."
why_it_matters_hint: The IMF chief links AI-driven investment and borrowing to debt risk that could hit governments and households.
notes: Two wire copies read (AP via Bozeman Daily Chronicle; The Business Standard/TBS, same speech). Original AP page blocked (403), so the AP link is given as the url. Pool score 7 kept: speech read in full, no overstatement. Category POL chosen (government policy on debt and AI rules).
